text:
Casey Cizikas has spent his whole career doing the jobs that don't make highlight packages, so it fit that his 1,000th NHL game ended with him blocking a Moritz Seider one-timer in the final minute, as NHL.com's Stefen Rosner described it. He also got a point: the secondary assist on Ondrej Palat's second goal was awarded to him after the fact. The Islanders won 3-2, and they deserved to.

Detroit led early on a goal it had no business scoring. Emmitt Finnie, the forward whose likeness replaced Dylan Larkin's on an arena banner this week, as the Detroit Free Press reported, beat Ilya Sorokin on a shot with under a 1% chance of going in, by our numbers. Larkin, the former captain, has been suspended without pay since late October after telling the team he would no longer play for it while he waits on a trade, and he remains the story hanging over every Red Wings game.

From there New York took over. Palat tipped in Ben Hutton's shot in the second to tie it. Simon Holmstrom put the Islanders ahead early in the third, extending his point streak to seven games, and Palat poked in a loose puck at 13:21 to make it 3-1. Alex DeBrincat answered at 13:50, but that was as close as Detroit got. Matthew Schaefer, the young defenseman who had a hat trick earlier in the week, assisted on both third-period goals in 25:48 of ice time.

The margin flatters Detroit. The Islanders had 3.93 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to 2.07, and in our replays of every shot they win this game 76% of the time. John Gibson is the reason it stayed close: he finished 0.56 goals better than expected and stopped Bo Horvat on an 86% chance in the third, the best look either team had all night. Sorokin was steady at the other end, 18 saves on 20.

Rosner's count has the Islanders at 11-6-5 and on a seven-game point streak (4-0-3). Detroit got a goal from DeBrincat and a strong night from Gibson, and still never really had the puck where it wanted it. Its biggest question remains unanswered off the ice.
headline: Cizikas gets his 1,000th-game point as Islanders hold on
